tagline: Through the land grant villages, one adobe church at a time.
intro: Out of Pojoaque the High Road crosses badlands of wind-carved hoodoos and dips into the green farming valley of Chimayó. From there NM 76 starts climbing into the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, up to Truchas on top of a high mesa and on through the old Las Trampas land grant, now national forest, from one small village to the next. Where NM 76 ends, with Picurís Pueblo a short turn to the left, the road takes NM 75 through Peñasco and Vadito, which means little ford.
It ends at Ranchos de Taos, at the church of San Francisco de Asís. Georgia O'Keeffe painted it several times, and the parish still turns out every year to replaster it with mud.

moments.title: El Santuario de Chimayó
moments.text: Pilgrims come to this adobe church of 1816 for a little holy dirt from a pit in a side room, and in the room next door discarded crutches are kept as testimony.

moments.title: Truchas
moments.text: A farming village of 1754 laid out around a walled plaza at 8,000 feet, under the snow-capped Truchas Peaks, that served as the set for the film of The Milagro Beanfield War.

moments.title: Las Trampas
moments.text: On a dirt plaza beside NM 76 stands San José de Gracia, finished in 1776, with adobe walls up to six feet thick and a clerestory window set to let sunlight into the apse.
